text:
anya: quick note from overnight shadow: fp8 variants show drift when we re-quant after a KV GC restore. small bias but reproducible on long-code prompts. examples uploaded to the shadow bucket.
marta: saw the same. hypothesis: stochastic rounding seed resets on restore -> subtle bias accumulates.
runtime-bot: traces: kv_restore -> requant(path=fp8) -> recompute. seed not persisted currently.
anya: if seed variability is the cause, two quick fixes: persist seed across restores or use deterministic rounding on restore. tradeoffs?
marta: deterministic rounding reduces drift but adds ~2-3ms per restore. persisting seed cheap but needs storage of per-tensor seed map and careful concurrency handling.
ops-kate: ops perspective: persisting seeds per-request increases metadata; sample at 1/500. deterministic rounding behind a route flag is easier for canaries.
eval-bot: quick sweep: deterministic rounding improved acceptability by ~4% on affected sets; persisting seeds removed ~80% of drift in repro cases.
anya: runtime implications: changing rounding mode mid-request requires kernel rebind on some backends (+12ms). for latency-sensitive routes we should prefer routing to an INT8-warmed lane instead of rebinding.
marta: propose policy: on KV-restore->requant detect if estimated rebind_cost >10ms AND route_p95<150ms -> route_to_int8_lane else perform local per-layer mlp-only int8 fallback first. add cooldown to avoid thrash.
ops-kate: agree. i'll add route config: requant_policy=[persist-seed|deterministic|route-prefer|no-autofallback] and customer lock to disable dynamic changes.
anya: action items: 1) runtime - add kv_restore tag + optional seed persist (marta, 4d) 2) ops - add route-level policy + customer lock (kate, 5d) 3) eval - prepare canary harness and sampled comparisons (eval-bot, 3d)
marta: will also add small microbench to measure rebind_cost per backend and expose metric rebind_latency_ms.
anya: schedule a non-prod canary next Tue 09:30 PT and reconvene after 24h. :thumbsup:
